title: Keyboard Manager shortcuts cannot override Windows shortcuts

judgment.rationale: The public reproduction proves a shell-hotkey conflict but cannot distinguish hook matching, suppression timing, injection failure, elevation, or settings state.
evidence: Win+Left and Win+Right mappings are reported to invoke Windows Snap.
Keyboard Manager already has a low-level hook and shortcut-to-key suppression path.
The reporter links older shortcut-remapping issues, but those concern intermittent failures rather than this immediate Win+Arrow conflict.
No diagnostic archive or hook/injection trace is supplied.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a fresh diagnostic and a focused comparison matrix before approving a code design.

fix_assessment.rationale: A product fix may apply, but the failing boundary is not proven; retain a red provisional investigation plan rather than inventing a root cause.

proposed_fixes.title: Instrument and isolate Win+Arrow remapping before changing suppression
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Provisional: the shell may receive Win+Arrow because the low-level hook misses or suppresses the physical event too late, or because replacement input fails; current evidence cannot choose among these.
plan: Capture hook initialization, settings load, match detection, modifier restoration, SendInput result, and suppression return for Win+Arrow.
Compare normal and elevated PowerToys, Snap enabled/disabled, and a non-shell Win shortcut.
Only after the trace identifies the boundary, add a narrowly scoped suppression or deferred injection fix and matching tests.
verification: The diagnostic matrix identifies whether matching, suppression, or injection is failing before implementation begins.

confidence.rationale: The current code suggests several plausible mechanisms and the issue lacks the evidence needed to select one.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager mappings for Win+Arrow do not prevent Windows Snap, but the report lacks the trace needed to identify where the remap path fails.
known_information: The report uses Win+Left to Home and Win+Right to End.
The actual result is Windows Snap left/right.
The affected versions include stable and preview builds on Windows 11.
The reporter linked issues 17344, 35730, and 17596; their reports concern shortcuts failing after use rather than immediate Win+Arrow handling.
inferences: The defect may be specific to shell-reserved Win+Arrow handling rather than all shortcut-to-key mappings.
A deferred injection design is only one possible fix and must not be implemented without a trace.
issue_context.analysis: Local code contains a nominal suppression path and existing tests, so changing it blindly could regress other mappings. A fresh bug report plus a small controlled matrix can distinguish hook installation, shortcut matching, physical suppression, and SendInput failure.
initial_investigation: Inspected KeyboardManager::HookProc, HandleKeyboardHookEvent, KeyboardEventHandlers::HandleShortcutRemapEvent, Shortcut modifier checks, and OS-level remapping tests.
Reviewed linked issues 17344, 35730, and 17596; they are not established duplicates because their reported failure occurs after use rather than on the first Win+Arrow press.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostic archive captured immediately after reproducing the Win+Arrow remap failure.
information_gaps.why_needed: The logs can show whether the hook initialized, the remap matched, or input injection failed.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce the Win+Arrow failure once, then add a comment containing /bugreport immediately afterward.

information_gaps.information: Results for normal versus elevated PowerToys, Windows Snap enabled versus disabled, and a control remap such as Win+A.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates shell-reserved shortcut behavior from a broader remap failure.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with a short comparison covering normal and elevated PowerToys, Snap enabled and disabled, and whether a control remap such as Win+A works.

comment.body:
The Win+Arrow reproduction and mappings are useful, but the current code already has a hook, suppression path, and injection path, so the next step is to identify which boundary is failing. Please provide:

1. A fresh PowerToys diagnostic archive: reproduce the Win+Arrow remap failure once, then add a comment containing "/bugreport" immediately afterward.
2. A short comparison of normal versus elevated PowerToys, Windows Snap enabled versus disabled, and a control remap such as Win+A, including whether each case works or still triggers the Windows shortcut.

design_decision.reason: Keep only lightweight red-confidence fix coverage until hook diagnostics arrive.

confidence.rationale: The current code suggests several plausible mechanisms and the issue lacks the evidence needed to select one.
